facts.raw_span: numerous whitish papules on the back of more than 10 years' duration
The lesions previously resolved with topical corticosteroids but flared soon after treatment discontinuation
Some papules became pruritic and extended to the waist and anterior trunk in the past month
No family history of similar lesions was recorded
Multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules on the back, waist, and inframammary area without genital involvement
Most lesions were folliculocentric under close inspection
Dermoscopy revealed central keratin plugs and some foci of structureless, whitish, and homogenous areas with surrounding erythema
Antinuclear antibody and hyperglobulinemia tests were negative
Biopsy specimen from back showed central follicular plug and epidermal atrophy covered by orthokeratotic stratum corneum
Papillary dermis was markedly thickened with homogenized collagens, areas of edema, and sparse bandlike lymphocytic infiltration
Some eosinophils in infiltrate and red blood cell extravasation
Congo red and mucicarmine stains were negative for amyloid and mucin

concepts.why: The presence of multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules on the back, waist, and inframammary area, along with dermoscopic findings of central keratin plugs and folliculocentric lesions, supports the diagnosis of lichen spinulosus.
The presence of folliculocentric papules and keratin plugs, along with the histopathologic finding of orthokeratotic stratum corneum, supports the diagnosis of keratosis pilaris.
The presence of pruritic papules and the histopathologic finding of bandlike lymphocytic infiltration supports the diagnosis of lichen planus.
The presence of scaly papules and the histopathologic finding of thickened papillary dermis supports the diagnosis of psoriasis.
The presence of dry, scaly skin and the histopathologic finding of orthokeratotic stratum corneum supports the diagnosis of ichthyosis.
The presence of pruritic papules and the histopathologic finding of bandlike lymphocytic infiltration supports the diagnosis of eczema.

The presence of multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules on the back, waist, and inframammary area, along with dermoscopic findings of central keratin plugs and folliculocentric lesions, supports the diagnosis of Darier disease.
The presence of folliculocentric papules and keratin plugs, along with the histopathologic finding of orthokeratotic stratum corneum, supports the diagnosis of keratosis follicularis.

rationales.F01: Numerous whitish papules on the back of more than 10 years' duration suggest a chronic condition, which could be consistent with Lichen spinulosus or Keratosis pilaris.
rationales.F02: The lesions' resolution with topical corticosteroids and subsequent flare after discontinuation may indicate a condition responsive to corticosteroids, such as Lichen spinulosus.
rationales.F06: Folliculocentric lesions are characteristic of Lichen spinulosus and Keratosis pilaris, making these conditions more likely.
rationales.F09: The biopsy specimen showing central follicular plug and epidermal atrophy covered by orthokeratotic stratum corneum is highly suggestive of Lichen spinulosus or Keratosis pilaris.
